project.name: fmt
project.commit_note: The staged ARVO workspace checkout at `_work/src/fmt` is on commit `6a1346405949ca1cf5befc5e83c6c66c86e4f9d1`, not the metadata `vulnerable_commit`. The line anchors below were resolved against that staged vulnerable tree, which still contains the unfixed `basic_memory_buffer::move` path without `other.clear()` shown in `patch.diff`.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42508600 (fmt): Stack-buffer-overflow READ 4 found by fuzz target one-arg-fuzzer [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42508600
bug_description.normalized: The staged 21-byte witness uses selector `0x0c` to route the one-arg fuzz harness into `invoke_fmt<long double>`, copies the next 16 bytes into the `long double` payload, and copies the remaining bytes into the exact format string `{:f}`. In fmt, `on_format_specs()` parses `f` as fixed-point formatting with the default precision 6, so `detail::write()` calls `format_float<long double>()` and the saved stack reaches `format_dragon()` line 2135, i.e. the negative-exponent branch. That branch calls `numerator.assign_pow10(-exp10)`, and by the crashing `square()` iteration `detail::bigint::bigits_` has already expanded beyond its inline 32-bigit capacity and is moved as a heap-backed `basic_memory_buffer<unsigned int, 32>`. The vulnerable move helper executes `other.set(other.store_, 0)` without clearing `other.size_`, rewiring the moved-from buffer to its inline store and zero capacity while leaving the old larger size intact. The immediately following resize re-enters `grow()`, whose `std::uninitialized_copy(old_data, old_data + this->size(), ...)` reads past the 32-element inline array, and AddressSanitizer reports a stack-buffer-overflow READ of size 4 from `format_dragon()`'s stack `numerator` object. The fix adds `other.clear()` after `other.set(other.store_, 0)` and a regression test that the moved-from dynamic buffer size becomes 0.

source.description: Scored source. After the selector has routed execution into the long-double arm, this is the first non-harness project statement that consumes attacker bytes into vulnerability-relevant state by copying the 16-byte payload into `repr` and materializing the `long double` later formatted by fmt.
source.value_from: After selector byte `0x0c`, the next 16 PoC bytes are `20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 00 00 20 20 20 20 20 20`. `assign_from_buf<Repr>` copies them verbatim into `repr`, and `value` aliases that materialized `long double` for later floating-formatting steps.

root_cause.description: Root cause. In the heap-backed move path, the moved-from `basic_memory_buffer` is rewired to its inline store and zero capacity but its old size is left intact, so the object becomes logically non-empty while pointing at only 32 inline `unsigned int` slots.
root_cause.note: `detail::buffer<T>::set()` only updates `ptr_` and `capacity_`; it does not reset `size_`. The patch adds `other.clear()` immediately after this line.

sink.description: Project-side crash site. `grow()` copies `this->size()` stale elements from the moved-from buffer's inline store, so the read runs past the 32-element array embedded in `format_dragon()`'s stack `numerator` object.
sink.note: AddressSanitizer's top frame is the inlined `std::__1::uninitialized_copy` implementation, and frame 1 is this `grow()` call at line 795.

tainted_value_origin.description: The harness copies the fixed-size post-selector payload into `repr`, and `value` aliases that materialized `long double`; the same object is later passed unchanged into `detail::write()` and `format_float<long double>()`.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: After selector byte `0x0c`, the next 16 bytes are `20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 00 00 20 20 20 20 20 20`. `assign_from_buf<Repr>` copies those bytes verbatim into the `long double` representation later consumed by the floating-format path.
tainted_value_origin.note: The remaining four bytes `7b 3a 66 7d` stay in `data/size` and become the exact format string in the next step.

parser_admitted.description: After selector `0x0c` has chosen the long-double arm, the harness has already materialized the 16-byte `long double` value and the 4-byte format string `"{:f}"`. This call enters the fmt library with those exact attacker-controlled inputs.

coarse_trace.function: LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput / invoke_fmt<long double, long double> / assign_from_buf / data_to_string
coarse_trace.summary: The harness reads selector `0x0c`, dispatches to the long-double arm, copies the next 16 bytes into the `long double` payload, and copies the trailing four bytes into the exact format string `{:f}`.
fmt parses `{:f}` into fixed-point formatting with default precision 6, computes a negative decimal exponent for the small-magnitude `long double`, and passes that state into `format_dragon()`.

In `format_dragon()`'s `exp10 < 0` branch, `assign_pow10(-exp10)` expands `numerator.bigits_` beyond the inline 32-bigit buffer; a later `square()` iteration moves that heap-backed buffer into a temporary and exposes the stale-size move bug.

coarse_trace.function: fmt::v8::basic_memory_buffer<unsigned int, 32ul, std::__1::allocator<unsigned int> >::move / fmt::v8::detail::buffer<unsigned int>::try_reserve / fmt::v8::basic_memory_buffer<unsigned int, 32ul, std::__1::allocator<unsigned int> >::grow
coarse_trace.summary: The vulnerable move path resets the moved-from buffer's pointer and capacity but not its size. The immediate resize then re-enters `grow()`, and `uninitialized_copy` overreads the 32-slot inline store from `format_dragon()`'s stack `numerator` object.

fine_trace.note: The first PoC byte is selector `0x0c`. The harness strips that byte from the buffer and `switch (first)` takes `case 12`, so the remaining 20 bytes are dispatched into `invoke_fmt<long double>()` on the crashing path.

Source. `assign_from_buf<Repr>` copies the first 16 post-selector bytes into `repr`, `value` aliases that materialized `long double`, and `data/size` advance past the fixed-size payload so only the trailing format bytes remain. This is the first non-harness statement that consumes attacker bytes into the floating value later used by `format_float()`.
The four remaining bytes `7b 3a 66 7d` are copied into a separate buffer and become the exact format string `"{:f}"` passed to fmt.

fmt parses the attacker-controlled format spec between `:` and `}`. For `"{:f}"`, this call records `specs.type = presentation_type::fixed_lower` and leaves `specs.precision = -1` because no explicit precision was supplied.

The long-double writer maps the parsed type into floating-format state. `fixed_lower` becomes `fspecs.format == float_format::fixed`, and because the witness supplied no explicit precision, fixed formatting uses the default precision 6 before calling `format_float()`.

For the materialized floating value from step 2 and the fixed-format state from step 5, `std::log10(value)` yields a negative decimal exponent. The saved stack reaches line 2291 here and line 2135 in `format_dragon()`, so this run keeps the Dragon path and passes a negative `exp` into `format_dragon()` rather than falling back to `snprintf_float`.

The saved `format_dragon()` frame is line 2135, so execution is in the `exp10 < 0` branch and `numerator.assign_pow10(-exp10)` starts building the power of ten for that negative exponent. The later root-cause line 730 only exists in the heap-backed move arm, so by the crashing squaring iteration this construction has already expanded `numerator.bigits_` past the inline 32-bigit storage.

During that `assign_pow10()` squaring iteration, `square()` moves the already heap-backed `bigits_` buffer into temporary `n`. That selects the heap-backed `basic_memory_buffer::move` arm rather than the inline-copy arm and exposes the moved-from object to the stale-size bug.

Root cause. In the heap-backed move arm, this rewires the moved-from buffer to its inline store with zero capacity, but `buffer::set()` does not touch `size_`. After this line the moved-from `bigits_` still carries its old nonzero length while pointing at only 32 inline `unsigned int` slots; the fix adds `other.clear()` here.

Immediately after the move, `square()` resizes the moved-from buffer for `num_result_bigits`. Because step 9 left `capacity_ == 0` and the requested count is positive, `try_reserve()` takes this branch and re-enters `grow()` while the stale size is still attached to the inline store.

Sink. `grow()` now sees `old_data == store_` from step 9, but `this->size()` is still the pre-move heap length. `uninitialized_copy` therefore reads past the end of the 32-element inline array and ASan reports the saved 4-byte stack-buffer-overflow from `format_dragon()`'s `numerator` object.

runtime_crash_location.function: unsigned int* std::__1::uninitialized_copy<unsigned int*, unsigned int*>(unsigned int*, unsigned int*, unsigned int*)

crash_stack.function: unsigned int* std::__1::uninitialized_copy<unsigned int*, unsigned int*>(unsigned int*, unsigned int*, unsigned int*)

cross_validation.patch_resolves_note: The staged fix adds `other.clear()` immediately after `other.set(other.store_, 0)` in `basic_memory_buffer::move`, so the moved-from buffer no longer keeps a stale nonzero size when `square()` resizes it. The accompanying regression test now expects the moved-from dynamic buffer size to be zero.

format.name: one-arg long-double fixed-format witness
format.contract: The only verified trigger semantics are the exact 21-byte witness saved in `poc` (SHA-256 `c74f7f1860528670be37ce26e70b9d16aeed14c296f29bd63ed055d2f8a8bc89`): selector byte `0c`, then the 16-byte long-double representation `20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 00 00 20 20 20 20 20 20`, then the four-byte format string `7b 3a 66 7d` (`"{:f}"`). In the staged run, selector `0x0c` reaches `invoke_fmt<long double>`, `"{:f}"` makes fmt use fixed-point formatting with default precision 6, and the saved ASan stack reaches `format_dragon()` line 2135, i.e. the `exp10 < 0` branch that calls `assign_pow10(-exp10)`. A later squaring iteration then hits the stale-size move/grow overread reported by ASan. This GT does not generalize beyond that exact witness.
